summary: Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (Republican) ran for re-election but lost to Scott Colom (Democrat), who was declared the winner on Nov. 11 after more than a week of counting.

candidates.name: Scott Colom
candidates.bio: Scott Colom is a Democrat born and raised in Columbus, Mississippi, who has worked as a prosecutor and a judge. He was first elected district attorney of Mississippi's 16th Judicial District in 2015 at age 32, unseating a 27-year incumbent. He announced his Senate campaign in September 2025.

positions.summary: Says he would vote to take back Congress's power over tariffs, fight to raise the minimum wage and tie it to the cost of living, and work to end the federal income tax for Mississippians making under $75,000.
Says he would vote to cancel the Medicaid cuts to help keep rural Mississippi's emergency and delivery rooms open, and restore the ACA tax credits that lower insurance premiums.
Says he would work to secure the border and enforce immigration laws.
Says he would push for a pause on new data center construction until the companies agree to pay for their own power and water.

candidates.name: Cindy Hyde-Smith
candidates.bio: Cindy Hyde-Smith is the Republican U.S. Senator from Mississippi and the first woman elected to represent the state in Congress. A graduate of Copiah-Lincoln Community College and the University of Southern Mississippi, she served 12 years in the state Senate and was elected state agriculture commissioner in 2011. She was appointed to the U.S. Senate in 2018 and won a full term in 2020.

positions.summary: Supports the Trump tax cuts and says she wants to cut federal regulations on small businesses, farmers and industry.
Favors changes that make insurance more affordable for Mississippi families without increasing federal involvement in care.
Supports nationwide E-Verify and cosponsored the Mandatory E-Verify Act of 2026.
Supports state and local control of public education, while recognizing a federal role in supporting educational achievement.
Says she supports responsible domestic energy exploration and production and new biofuel technologies.
Says she believes in the sanctity of life, opposes taxpayer-funded abortion, and chairs the Senate Pro-Life Caucus.

factCheckNote: AP called Colom the winner Nov 11 and Hyde-Smith conceded (CNN projected earlier); confirmed by AP-syndicated report and political.org tally. 2026-11-25: all shares are computed from the vote counts on the NBC News results page, last updated Nov. 19, 2026. State certification was not confirmed.
